newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi - Italy wants meet EMU criteria next spring.
newsitem.headline: Prodi - Italy wants meet EMU criteria next spring.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, expressing renewed confidence about Italy's chances to join the new European currency, said on Friday Italy will try to fulfil entry requirements for the European currency by next spring.
Prodi told Reuters Financial Television in an interview that he was more confident of Italy fulfilling criteria laid out in the Maastricht Treaty than he was weeks ago.

"Italy's task is harder than Germany's but I am more confident than I was a few weeks ago," Prodi said. "There is no possibility that Italy will not be there for consideration for currency union on time."

Prodi said Italy will be an asset rather than a liability for the euro, seeking to downplay concerns that Italy's membership in the currency could create turmoil in financial markets amid doubts about the currency's strength.
"If we join, we shall join using correct behaviour within the correct parameters," Prodi said. "Italy will be a strength for the euro, not a weakness."

Prodi made the comments in an interview following a one-day summit with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl to discuss Italy's future in the planned European currency. Both leaders said there was no rift between Bonn and Rome over currency union.
Prodi said Italy had demonstrated its commitment to convincing financial markets of its suitability by taking the necessary political steps to shore up its finances.
"They have already touched on all the parts of my budget," he said of the reforms.
